title: RSL Companion consolidated account export
description: Payload POSTed to {ApiBaseUrl}/api/sync/consolidated/raw. One complete snapshot of one game account; a full replace, not a delta. Self-identifying: the server routes by the in-game accountId it carries. Human-readable contract and changelog: export-schema.md (keep both in sync, same commit).

x-relatedSchemas.clan: clan-export-schema.json — the account's clan record and roster; a SEPARATE payload to a separate endpoint, joined to this one on clanId.

x-relatedCatalogs.roles: role-names.json — heroes[].roleId to role name. Static game metadata (the HeroRole enum), shipped here because roleId is an opaque int without it.
x-relatedCatalogs.artifacts: artifact-enums.json — artifacts[]/accessories[] kindId (slot), statKindId, rankId and setKindId to names. Static game metadata (the ArtifactKindId / StatKindId / ArtifactRankId / ArtifactSetKindId enums).
x-relatedCatalogs.relics: relic-enums.json — relics[].sockets[].shapeKindId to socket shape. Relic and gemstone typeId are NOT named there: they are a catalog of the game (name, rarity, group, skill, stat bonuses) and belong in a champion-metadata-style catalog keyed on typeId.

accountId.description: In-game account id. The routing key; always equals account.accountId.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the snapshot was taken.

uploaderVersion.description: Desktop app build that produced this payload. Stamped by the app, NOT by the extraction engine, so it is absent from engine-level dumps.

gameVersion.description: Live Raid build the snapshot was read from. Null when it could not be determined.

accountId.description: Duplicate of the top-level accountId; always equal.

resources.description: ALWAYS the complete allowlist (49 ids as of schema 3). Ids the account holds none of are present with quantity 0, so a missing id means the allowlist changed - never 'zero owned'. Join on id, NEVER on name: names track in-game renames (three changed in v1.5.4). NEVER ALL-ZERO: because every id is emitted unconditionally, a failed read returns a full-length array of zeroes rather than an empty one - so length proves nothing here and the `contains` constraint above is the real check. Every account holds at least some Silver, so at least one quantity is always non-zero. The uploader refuses to send an all-zero array; a consumer seeing one should discard the payload and keep what it has, never apply it (applying it zeroes the account's entire inventory).

id.description: Stable allowlist id. The only safe join key.

name.description: Display label. NOT stable across releases.

x-soulEconomy.description: Corrected in schema 3 / v1.5.4. Ids 10101, 10102, 10104, 10105, 10201 and 10204 are a DEFUNCT earlier soul system: they are not allowlisted, are never emitted, and must not be mapped onto the ids below - doing so is the bug v1.5.4 fixed.

ids.1111: Mortal Soul Coin (was 'Silver Soul Coin'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.1112: Immortal Soul Coin (was 'Gold Soul Coin'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.1113: Eternal Soul Coin (was 'Immortal Essence'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.10205: Eternal Essence (legacy; still emitted, semantics unverified)

heroes.description: The owned champion roster. NEVER EMPTY: the game gives every new player a starter champion, so there is no such thing as an account with zero. A zero-length array is therefore a failed read, not an empty roster — the uploader refuses to send one, and this constraint makes a consumer reject it rather than faithfully applying it and wiping the account's champions. Treat a validation failure here as 'discard this payload and keep what you have'.

name.description: Null when the champion index cannot resolve it.

instanceId.description: int64. Unique per OWNED COPY. Join key for factionGuardians and artifacts.

baseTypeId.description: Champion type, ascension digit stripped. Copies of one champion share this.

factionId.description: 0 when unresolved. Same id space as factionGuardians[].factionId.

roleId.description: Champion role: 0 Attack, 1 Defense, 2 Health (shown as 'HP'), 3 Support, 4 Evolve, 5 Xp. NULL — never 0 — when unresolved, because 0 is a real role. Static per champion, NOT per copy: it is the game's HeroRole enum on the shared champion type, so every copy of a champion reports the same value and the id table is game metadata (role-names.json), not account data. Null on roughly a fifth of a mature roster because the client hydrates a champion's type lazily; prefer a champion metadata catalog keyed on baseTypeId as the authoritative source, and treat this field as a convenience copy.

blessingChosen.description: A blessing is equipped. Only ever true when awakeningLevel > 0.

isFactionGuardian.description: This copy is placed in an Academy guardian slot.

skills.description: This copy's skills and how far each is upgraded, sorted by typeId. Always present; empty only on a failed read (every champion has at least one skill). Per-skill metadata - name, description, cooldown, and the MAXIMUM level - is intentionally absent: it is constant game data, joined on typeId from a skill catalog. Without that catalog 'level 5' cannot be read as maxed or not.

typeId.description: Skill type id, and the catalog join key. TREAT AS OPAQUE - join it, do not derive it. It is usually baseTypeId*10 + slot (Kael, base 1510 -> 15101..15104) and is stable across copies and ascensions, but two documented exceptions break any derivation: a champion with a second form ALSO carries that form's block at 800000 + the own-block id (10 champions, 53 skills on the mapping account, which is why skills[] can hold 10-12 entries), and a skill can belong to another champion's id block entirely (Ezio Auditore and Edward Kenway both carry 102505). Slots are also not dense: a 3-skill champion may report 15101/15103/15104.

level.description: Upgrade level, 1-BASED. 1 means un-upgraded, so books applied = level-1. Observed range 1-9; the cap is per-skill and lives in the catalog, not here.

masteries.description: Always present and fully populated - deliberately verbose so consumers never null-check. Per-node metadata (name/tree/tier/cost) is intentionally absent: it is constant game data, joined from mastery_index.json in the RslCompanionMetadata repo.

selected.description: Chosen mastery node ids; empty array when none, never null. The id encodes position: 500*tree*tier*slot, tier being the tens digit.

totalScrolls.description: Unspent PLUS already spent on selected (each node's activation cost).

factionGuardians.description: Academy guardian slots. Each slot fuses up to TWO copies of one champion, hence the First/Second pair.

heroTypeId.description: Champion type WITH the ascension digit (366 = base 360 at ascension 6). Do NOT join this onto heroes[].baseTypeId.

heroBaseTypeId.description: Ascension stripped. THIS is what joins to heroes[].baseTypeId. The game's own field is misleadingly named HeroBaseTypeId but carries the ascension digit; both forms are published so consumers need not guess.

firstHeroInstanceId.description: Null when that half of the slot is empty.

secondHeroInstanceId.description: Null when that half of the slot is empty.

artifacts.description: GEAR the account owns - helmet, chest, gloves, boots, weapon, shield (kindId 1-6) - equipped AND vaulted, with real stats. Rings/cloaks/banners are NOT here; they are in accessories[]. BREAKING CHANGE IN SCHEMA 9: through schema 8 this array was the equipped-artifact MAP across all nine slots with every stat field hard-zero, and consumers were told a 0 meant 'unknown'. Both of those are now false - the array is an OWNED list (2851 gear on the reference account, 1963 of them unequipped), accessories have moved out, and a 0 is a real 0. Three migration traps: reading this array for accessories now silently finds none; array length is an owned count, not an equipped count (test equippedByHeroId != null for that); and code that gates writes on 'stat != 0' will now drop legitimate zeroes. RECONCILING WITH THE GAME: length equals the in-game gear total exactly, and the count with equippedByHeroId == null equals the in-game unequipped total exactly - measured live 2026-08-02 at 2851 / 1963. Those are a SNAPSHOT, not constants - they move whenever the player farms, sells or equips (the same account eight hours earlier gave 2811 / 1922). What holds is the relationship, tested against counters read at the same moment. The one category still absent is the MAILBOX: unclaimed items belong to no inventory until collected and are counted in neither this array nor the in-game counter it reconciles against. May legitimately be empty on a brand-new account.

accessories.description: Rings, cloaks and banners (kindId 7-9) the account owns, equipped AND vaulted. Identical record shape to artifacts[]; new in schema 9, where these records were previously mixed into artifacts[] as ids without stats. Kept separate because the game keeps them separate (their own inventory and their own counter), because a consumer rarely needs gear and accessories in the same request, and so the server can store and serve the two independently. Note accessories are faction-locked: requiredFactionId is non-zero on all of them (2969 of 2969 on the reference account), where gear is unrestricted. Reconciles exactly against the in-game accessory counters - measured live 2026-08-02: 2969 total, 2000 with equippedByHeroId == null. Those numbers are a snapshot of one account at one moment, not constants - see the note on artifacts[].

relics.description: Every RELIC the account owns, equipped AND in storage, each with its gemstone sockets. New in schema 11; nothing resembling it existed before, so there is no migration - a consumer that ignores the array is exactly as correct as it was in schema 10. Its own array rather than part of artifacts[] because relics are a separate inventory in game, with their own counters, their own id space and their own upgrade currencies (Basalt and Starstone, both new resource ids in this schema). RECONCILING WITH THE GAME: length equals the in-game relic total and the count with equippedByHeroId == null equals the in-game unequipped total - measured live 2026-08-03 at 377 total / 240 unequipped / 137 equipped. A SNAPSHOT, not constants: check the relationship against counters read at the same moment, never the literals. One relic per champion is what this account shows (137 relics across 137 heroes, none with two), but that is an observation about the game's current rules, not a guarantee the payload enforces - the field is a per-relic hero reference, so handle a hero appearing twice.

gemstones.description: Every GEMSTONE the account owns, socketed AND in storage. The game class is RelicStone; the UI calls them gemstones. Separate from relics[] for the reason accessories[] is separate from artifacts[]: the game counts them as their own inventory, and MOST OF THEM ARE IN NO RELIC AT ALL - 303 of 543 on the reference account. Nesting them under the relic holding them would have hidden 56% of the inventory, which is the same shape of loss that made schema 8's equipped-only artifacts[] look plausible while missing two thirds of the data. Joins to relics[] both ways: a socket's stoneId is a gemstones[].id, and that gemstone's socketedInRelicId points back at the relic. Measured live 2026-08-03: 543 total, 240 socketed, 303 free; both directions of the join agreed on all 240 with no dangling reference.

clanId.description: int64 id of the clan this account belongs to (the game calls a clan an Alliance). Null when the account is in no clan AND when the value could not be validated — this payload cannot distinguish the two, so never infer 'left the clan' from null. Stable and usable as a join key on its own: two accounts in the same clan report the same clanId. It is the ONLY clan field here because it is the only free one — a two-pointer read off the account data — whereas the clan's name and roster need a full-memory scan of the game (18-31s on a ~4s export) and are therefore a separate export: see clan-export-schema.json, which joins to this on clan.id.

artifact.description: One owned artifact. The same shape backs artifacts[] (gear) and accessories[]; kindId decides which array it lands in. Every field is read from the game's own record, so a 0 is a real 0 - unlike schemas 7-8, nothing here is a placeholder.

artifactId.description: Instance id, unique across BOTH arrays, and stable for the life of the piece (it survives upgrades and re-equips) - so it is the join key for change detection.

kindId.description: Slot, from the game's ArtifactKindId enum: 1 Helmet, 2 Chest, 3 Gloves, 4 Boots, 5 Weapon, 6 Shield, 7 Ring, 8 Cloak (the UI calls it Amulet), 9 Banner. WARNING: schemas 7-8 documented a DIFFERENT and incorrect order (1 Weapon, 2 Helmet, 3 Shield, 4 Gauntlets, 5 Chestplate); a consumer that hard-coded those labels is mislabelling slots. The order above is the enum's own, corroborated by which primary stat each slot always rolls. Names: artifact-enums.json.

setKindId.description: TWO ID SPACES IN ONE FIELD. 0-66 are artifact SETS, where 0 means NO SET - a real value, not 'unknown'. 1000-1004 are ACCESSORY EFFECTS: one item's own effect, with no piece count and no set bonus, occurring on ~2.6% of accessories and on no gear. Grouping 'by set' across the 1000s invents five sets that do not exist. Join on the id, never the name - Cleansing, Bloodshield, Reaction and Revenge occur in both spaces. Both tables: artifact-enums.json (`sets` and `accessoryEffects`). The set names published before 2026-08-02 were wrong from id 4 onward; re-derive any stored labels.

level.description: Upgrade level. 0 is a real, common value (an un-upgraded drop).

ascendLevel.description: Ascension level. ascendBonus is non-null exactly when this is > 0.

requiredFactionId.description: Faction the piece is locked to; 0 = unrestricted. Same id space as heroes[].factionId. Non-zero on every accessory, zero on gear.

equippedByHeroId.description: int64. The hero instance id wearing this piece, joining to heroes[].instanceId - or NULL when it sits in the vault, which is the majority of records. Null means 'not equipped', never 'wearer unknown'. This replaces schema 8's heroInstanceId, which was non-null on every record because only equipped artifacts were exported.

price.description: Silver cost of the next upgrade.

failedUpgrades.description: Failed upgrade attempts since the last success - the game's pity counter.

revision.description: Server-side revision of this record, bumped when the game changes it. Lets a sync diff instead of rewriting the whole vault.

primaryBonus.description: Always present. Replaces schema 8's primaryStatId, which was always 0 and carried no value alongside it.

ascendBonus.description: The bonus granted by ascension; null unless ascendLevel > 0.

relic.description: One owned relic. ACCOUNT STATE ONLY: a relic's name, rarity, group, skill and stat bonuses live on the shared RelicType, which is a catalog of the game rather than anything about this player - the same split that keeps skill names and mastery-node metadata out of heroes[]. Join those on typeId.

id.description: Instance id, unique within the account and stable across upgrades and re-equips - the join key for change detection, and what a socket's stoneId is NOT (that is a gemstone id, a different space).

typeId.description: The shared RelicType this is a copy of; the join key into a relic catalog. Opaque - 57 distinct values in range 1-86 on the reference account. NOT named in relic-enums.json: the game ships l10n:relic/name?id=N keys but this client build has no localized strings behind them and falls back to placeholder text ('Relic 12 name'), so no honest name table can be built from memory today. Gemstone type names DO resolve.

rank.description: 1-5 observed. Raising a relic from rank N to N+1 is paid for in Rank N Basalt, resource id 19000+N - which is why there are exactly five Basalt ranks. Rank 6 exists as an upgrade target ('Used to upgrade a Rank 5 Relic to Rank 6') but no rank-6 relic occurred on the reference account, so the upper bound is deliberately not constrained here.

level.description: Upgrade level, paid for in Starstone (resource id 4000). Observed 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 - it steps by 3, and 0 is a real and common value (213 of 377). Do not assume every integer in the range occurs.

equippedByHeroId.description: int64. Hero instance id wearing this relic, joining to heroes[].instanceId - or NULL when it is in storage, which is most of them. Null means 'not equipped', never 'wearer unknown'.

sockets.description: The relic's gemstone sockets in the game's own order. 1-4 per relic (170/149/55/3 on the reference account). Count and shapes are fixed by the relic's type; what varies per copy is which are filled.

relicSocket.description: One gemstone socket. A gemstone only fits a socket of its own shape, so shapeKindId is what decides what can go in.

shapeKindId.description: Socket shape, the game's RelicStoneShapeKindId enum. Names in relic-enums.json - but read the provenance note there before using them: the enum's five members are Circle, Triangle, Square, Diamond, Pentagon and the observed values are exactly 1-5, yet the member-to-value binding is inferred from DECLARATION ORDER and is not independently confirmed. Treat the id as authoritative and the label as provisional.

stoneId.description: The gemstones[].id socketed here, or NULL when the socket is empty. Null is the common case (405 of 645 sockets). This is a gemstone instance id and does NOT join to relics[].id.

gemstone.description: One owned gemstone (game class RelicStone). ACCOUNT STATE ONLY, same split as relics[]: name, rarity, shape and skill hang off the shared RelicStoneType and are joined on typeId.

id.description: Instance id - what relics[].sockets[].stoneId points at.

typeId.description: The shared RelicStoneType; the join key into a gemstone catalog. 68 distinct values on the reference account. Unlike relic type names, these DO resolve from the game's l10n table (l10n:relic-stone/name?id=N, 120 ids) - they are still catalog data and so are not shipped in the payload.

socketedInRelicId.description: The relics[].id this gemstone sits in, or NULL when it is in storage. Derived by inverting the sockets, so it is exactly consistent with them by construction - it is a convenience for consumers that index gemstones directly, not a second source of truth.

artifactBonus.description: One stat line. isAbsolute decides how value reads: true = a flat amount (+240 ATK), false = a FRACTION of the champion's base stat (0.18 = +18%, NOT 0.18%). The value comes from the game's 64-bit fixed-point storage divided by 2^31 and rounded to 6 decimals, so a relative value may exceed 1.0 (1.6 = +160% critical damage on a maxed banner) - do not validate it as a 0-1 probability. NOT exported: the game's _powerUpValue / _rarityBasedPowerUpValue / _powerUpRarityId, which are the upgrade screen's preview of the next roll and are null on every record of a snapshot taken with that screen closed.

statKindId.description: Game enum StatKindId: 1 Health, 2 Attack, 3 Defence, 4 Speed, 5 Resistance, 6 Accuracy, 7 CriticalChance, 8 CriticalDamage, 9 CriticalHeal, 10 IgnoreDefence. Only 1-8 occur on artifacts. Names: artifact-enums.json.

value.description: Flat amount when isAbsolute, otherwise a fraction (0.18 = 18%).

level.description: How many times this substat has been rolled up. 0 is a real value (never upgraded), not 'missing'.

scrollBalance.description: Mastery-scroll balance. ALWAYS carries all three rarities, defaulting to 0.
